body:
openChannelImpl declares its pool with no membership and no admit, so openSeparate's reseed
federates the receiver's WHOLE root ground into the pool, on every attach including boot
(openChannelImpl's pool declaration in src/federation/channel.ts (~732-741 on main; anchor by function name, lines drift), src/gateway/container.ts ~1217-1227). Four measured
consequences (T203/T204 builds, 2026-08-21):
1. A channel pool's container page lists the primary's constitutional deltas — users, roles,
   grants, the OTHER channels' records — as members.
2. A root binding published under a channel's prefix lands in the pool at attach, and the
   replay fold re-aggregates the root's own binding as a CHANNEL row with the channel's origin
   rank.
3. A struck root policy declaration keeps governing the pool: the pool holds a copy taken at
   attach time and no strike crosses that edge (H1 at the container seam).
4. T204's reboot case: the pool's reader names a contest against the root's own binding-copy;
   the contested reading is honest against it (the serving contender is marked by content
   address), but the underlying state is wrong.

The fix changes WHAT BINDS in a pool, so the decision is design-shaped: the candidate is
declaring the pool with an admit/membership that seeds nothing (a channel pool's ground should
hold the peer's deltas, the receiver's blessings, and the custody stamps — not a root mirror),
plus a migration story for pools already seeded. Draft the analysis, recommend, and STOP for
Myk — §46/§47 ground.

Acceptance criteria (for the design phase):
(a) A working-spec amendment or ticket-body decision from Myk on the pool's seeding contract,
    with the migration for existing pools named. Verify: Myk's word in chat or PR review;
    the build criteria are written then.

Merge tier: DESIGN-STAGE — Myk's merge. Do not build past the analysis without his word.
title: A channel pool is seeded with a full copy of the root ground — and no strike crosses the seam
